correctness.rationale: For each of exactly \(2^{\ell(n-1)}\) prefixes, the augmented distance when the free column changes in \(t\) bits is \(t+(t\bmod2)\), so any two free columns of Hamming distance one or two have overlapping single-error balls. Thus every fiber is an \(\ell\)-bit distance-three code. Conversely, row-parity words in a maximum classical distance-three seed yield exactly \(2^{\ell(n-1)}A_2(\ell,3)\) matrices; row-length detection recovers insertion/deletion, and column parity plus uniquely nearest seed parity recovers substitutions. All quantified \(n>\ell\ge2\) are covered by this formal argument. The attached standard-library verifier exhaustively checks three representative SID constructions, Hamming-distance lemmas for \(\ell\le8\), small classical optima, and 190 seed pairs at \(\ell=8\). Finite checks are corroboration, not a proof of the universal statement.

The new fiberwise sharp upper bound and resulting exact all-\(\ell\) identity are not stated or implied by those inequalities; the difference is strict for \(\ell=8\), where classical \(A_2(8,3)=20\) versus \(2^8/9\) sphere capacity. value.rationale: This resolves the explicit within-one-bit optimality gap for the one-edit sum channel for every eligible number of rows and frame length, expressing exact maximum cardinality through the classical one-error-correcting code invariant. Theorem proves even substitution-only codes cannot exceed the same maximum, which is useful in RAID-style striped parity storage and low-rate DNA coding. An established nonlinear \((8,20,3)\) seed improves input-code cardinality by 25% over the original shortened-Hamming choice; no misstatement about fixed-length indexing or new classical seed optimality is made.
